Round 2 · Implementation · Medium

Ticket #14 — Checkout Promotion Engine

Difficulty: Medium

Context

You maintain price quotes for a campus shop. A cart line is (sku, quantity, unit_price_cents); a SKU identifies one product. Promotions may apply to a set of eligible SKUs and require a minimum whole-cart subtotal. A quote returns subtotal, discount, tax, and total, all in cents.

Practice report

Configure SAVE10 as 10 percent off books, with a 5000-cent minimum. Quote one 6000-cent book and one excluded 4000-cent pen, with tax rate 0.

Observation Current starter Expected
Cart subtotal 10000 10000
Discount 1000 600
Total 9000 9400

The customer should receive the promotion only on eligible merchandise.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Validate line quantities and prices: quantities must be positive and unit prices nonnegative; an invalid line raises ValueError without changing the promotion store.
  • Determine minimum spend from the full cart subtotal. A missing/unknown code, insufficient spend, or a cart with no eligible products gives no discount.
  • Percentage promotions apply to the eligible subtotal, using the existing whole-cent floor calculation. Fixed promotions cannot exceed that eligible subtotal; an empty eligible-SKU set means all products are eligible.
  • Subtract the discount before calculating tax, retaining the existing round(taxable_amount * tax_rate) behavior. Total equals taxable amount plus tax and cannot become negative for the supplied valid promotion/tax inputs.
  • Quotes do not modify the cart or saved promotions. A 6000-cent eligible cart with a 600-cent discount and tax rate 0.1 yields tax 540 and total 5940.

Out of Scope

Keep the quote API, existing rounding, and configured promotion data. Promotion stacking, shipping charges, tax jurisdiction rules, and new rate-validation policies are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the mixed cart, then compare it with eligible-only and excluded-only carts. Add regression assertions for every quote field, minimum spend, and a fixed discount larger than the eligible value. Explain how the results satisfy the pricing contract without changing rounding behavior.
